source.title: The Low-Rank Simplicity Bias in Deep Networks
source.authors: Minyoung Huh; H. Mobahi; Richard Zhang; Brian Cheung; Pulkit Agrawal; Phillip Isola

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different parameterization of deep networks affects generalization, using linear over-parameterization and image-classification accuracy rather than the interventions or measures in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own natural-image classification results for linear over-parameterization and explicit regularizers. Its least-squares experiments and low-rank measurements use synthetic tasks; they do not test the listed versions. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests generalization effects of depth and functionally equivalent linear reparameterization, but none of V1–V8. It does not sweep width beyond interpolation, compare convolutional with fully connected classifiers, or measure magnitude-aware sharpness. Its optimizer comparisons measure embedding rank on synthetic regression, not the held-out benchmark performance named in V4. Its discussion of random-label memorization does not test or contradict V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors empirically observe a depth-related bias toward lower effective-rank embeddings and conjecture that increasing parameter-space volume for such embeddings explains it. Linear expansion can improve natural-image generalization without changing functional capacity, while excessive depth or high-rank targets can make the bias harmful.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies linear over-parameterization of existing layers and low-rank embedding measurements; its main natural-image intervention is not one of the versions' listed procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect of linear over-parameterization depends on expansion factor, architecture depth, and dataset; gains diminish with deeper ImageNet models, and models starting from ResNet34 perform worse than the original. Explicit regularization comparisons also vary by dataset and regularizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Functionally equivalent linear expansion improves CIFAR and ImageNet classification accuracy in the recorded configurations. Benefits diminish with original architecture depth; Section 4.1 reports worse performance starting from ResNet34.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear expansion by depth can improve image-classification generalization without increasing functional capacity, with benefits depending on architecture and expansion factor.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic regression experiments show lower effective-rank embeddings with greater depth across several optimizers. Whether depth improves held-out loss depends on task rank and noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth biases networks toward lower effective-rank embeddings, which can help or hurt generalization depending on the target mapping and observation noise.

record.problems: The ImageNet table reports no uncertainty. Classification variability is reported only as < 0.3% for individual runs, without per-configuration error bars. Figure 7 provides qualitative train/test dynamics without exact values in the text. Several synthetic least-squares experiments do not directly establish natural-label generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional natural-image classification configurations from Table 1 are included; its flattened configuration marks and accuracy columns make some FC/Conv expansion assignments difficult to recover reliably. Cited results and synthetic least-squares findings are excluded from result rows.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments, including chance-level held-out performance for random labels.
Test-error changes from widening networks beyond the width needed for zero training error. The brief expansion-width observation provides no interpolation-threshold comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, the contribution of local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance on image or language benchmarks under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with generalization gaps, and their ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of examples selected by label memorization versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded values concern a finding outside V1–V8, so their states are cannot_determine relative to those versions. The record's tests/T2 classification should be replaced with discusses/T6. No missing result bearing on a listed version was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on image or language benchmarks.
Large- versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
